reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 15x15 grid of 5x5 blocks: the middle 3x3 blocks are the input upscaled x3 (each fg cell a solid block), and a copy of the input is placed in every outer-ring block that is 4-adjacent to a solid block.

slots.core: input scaled x3, placed at block offset (1,1)
slots.copies: input copied into each ring block edge-adjacent to a solid core block (edge cells give one, corner cells two, centre none)

why: every 3x3 block is solid fg, a copy of the input, or empty; copies appear exactly in ring blocks touching a solid block

reading: Each colour-4 shape sits against a vertical colour-2 line; a single marker cell of another colour lies on the other side. The shape is mirrored across the 2-line and the mirrored copy is drawn in the marker's colour.

slots.subject: each 4-coloured shape touching a 2-line
slots.colour: the marker cell on the opposite side of that line (marker lies inside the reflected footprint)

why: every mirrored cell is the reflection of a shape cell across its 2-line and has the marker colour; originals unchanged

reading: Stray 8 cells inside the 2-region become 2; stray 8 cells inside the 7-region stay and add one more 8 one step toward the edge that is a full line of 9.

slots.subject: colour-8 cells
slots.rule_in_7: keep and paint the neighbour toward the 9 border line with 8
slots.direction: side of the grid that is a full 9 line

why: 8s whose neighbours are mostly 2 become 2; every other 8 gains exactly one 8 neighbour on the 9-border side
invariants: 2 and 7 cells other than the painted step

reading: From each 6 on the bottom row a 2-line climbs; just below a horizontal 7-segment it marks 4, puts 8 on the segment above, runs 2s right under the segment to one past its end where it marks 3, then climbs again, ending at the top (marked 6) or at a gap.

slots.path: 2 cells going up, detouring right under each horizontal 7 bar it meets
slots.turn marks: 4 at detour start, 8 on the bar above it, 3 at the corner past the bar end
slots.end: 6 at the top edge or under a closed gap

why: every added cell lies on the climb-and-detour path from a 6

reading: Four 4-coloured corner cells mark a window; crop it and complete the large partial pattern inside as a scaled-up copy of the small multicolour exemplar found elsewhere in the input.

slots.window: box spanned by the four 4 corner cells (inclusive)
slots.exemplar: small multicolour component outside the window
slots.scale: ratio between the large pieces in the window and the exemplar
slots.placement: aligned so the existing large pieces coincide with the scaled exemplar

why: output = window crop with the scaled exemplar painted where its existing pieces fit

reading: Count the cells of each non-background colour; each count is a perfect square n*n, drawn as an n x n square. Squares are laid left to right in ascending size, bottom-aligned, separated by one background column, height = largest side.

slots.subject: each non-background colour
slots.layout: ascending left to right, bottom-aligned, 1-column bg gaps

why: each colour's square area equals its input cell count

reading: Each solid rectangle holds one marker cell of another colour; its interior is cleared to 0 (outline kept) and an X is drawn from the four interior corners inward along the diagonals in the marker colour.

slots.subject: each solid rectangle with one odd-colour marker
slots.rest: interior cleared to background, outline kept
slots.line: diagonals from the interior corners toward the centre, marker colour

why: every interior cell is either on a corner diagonal (marker colour) or background

reading: The 3x3 input becomes a 9x9 grid of 3x3 blocks; each block whose input cell is background gets the colour-inverted input (fg<->bg swapped), the others stay empty.

slots.unit: the input with its fg colour and background swapped
slots.extent: blocks at the input's background cells (tile extent=bg)

why: every block is the inverted input or empty; inverted copies exactly at input background positions

reading: Three 3x3 panels are separated by 5-columns; the first holds a pattern, the second gets it rotated 90 degrees clockwise and the third rotated 180 degrees.
why: panel k equals the source rotated by (k-1)*90 degrees clockwise

reading: The 8-figure is built on a 4x4 block lattice anchored at its top-left fg cell; every background cell inside a 4x4 block that contains any 8 is filled with 2.

new_rows.name: blockbg
new_rows.datalog:
gy0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gx0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
lo(0, 0). lo(1, 4). lo(2, 8). lo(3, 12). lo(4, 16). lo(5, 20). lo(6, 24). lo(7, 28).
rb(Y, B) :- px(Y, X, C), gy0(Y0), lo(B, L), Y1 = Y0 + L, Y2 = Y1 + 3, Y >= Y1, Y <= Y2.
cb(X, B) :- px(Y, X, C), gx0(X0), lo(B, L), X1 = X0 + L, X2 = X1 + 3, X >= X1, X <= X2.
hot(BY, BX) :- cell(Y, X, C), rb(Y, BY), cb(X, BX).
blockbg(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), rb(Y, BY), cb(X, BX), hot(BY, BX).

why: every background cell in an occupied 4x4 block becomes 2; nothing else changes
